pr_title: [AudioTrack RAW] Fix TrueHD and DD+ broken after pause or seek also fixes audio keep alive in all platforms
pr_body:
## Description
Fixes:
- TrueHD and DD+ broken after pause or seek in AudioTrack RAW (Android only).
- Audio keep alive broken when setting is "Always" (all platforms).

Closes https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/22230
Closes https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/21317

For clarification does NOT fixes:
- Audio keep alive settings changes not apply without restart Kodi.
- TrueHD random dropouts using AudioTrack IEC (in case of users suffering from this issue).

## Motivation and context
Keep alive is broken mainly because overflow in INT_MAX value multiplied for 60000 to convert to ms here:

https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/077c7888fc58c05f27f061e306068cacb95843d2/xbmc/cores/AudioEngine/Engines/ActiveAE/ActiveAE.cpp#L2665

This is 128,849,018,820,000 which is not possible in a signed int :)

But also other bad things:

`std::chrono::milliseconds` type variables are not default zero initialized:

![not-initialized](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/58434170/209941779-e202d4d1-781d-4549-9395-ab40b584e8d3.png)

Also in Android AudioTrack RAW only keep alive feature breaks TrueHD RAW stream because is not possible insert silence frames in middle of stream (possible is but not easy).

TrueHD is a complex format and some audio frames depends of previous audio frames, inserting zero data frames in essence corrupts the stream. At least must be necessary generate correct silence frames with correct config flags, length and CRCs followed by major_sync_frame of stream (not any random point of stream). This requires at least partial parse of raw stream same as IEC:

https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/077c7888fc58c05f27f061e306068cacb95843d2/xbmc/cores/AudioEngine/Utils/AEBitstreamPacker.cpp#L190-L201

And sync cut points with next major_sync_frame

In the other hand with more simple audio formats as DTS this works because all audio frames are playable by itself (not requires previous special frames).

As simple workaround this PR disables inserting silence only in AudioTrack RAW + TrueHD or DD+. 
This introduces a small gap of time (less 1s) without audio after the pause or seek but is much better than the audio never coming back (or it returns intermittently because the stream is corrupted).

For the AVR it is as if the stream has ended (while it's paused or seeking) and when unpaused it starts synchronizing with the next major_sync_frame.


## How has this been tested?
Runtime tested Shield Pro 2019 + Denon X1600H


## What is the effect on users?
- Fixes TrueHD and DD+ broken after pause or seek in AudioTrack RAW (Android only).
- Fixes audio keep alive broken when setting is "Always" (all platforms).

Take care for the silence generation in RAW. We don't create them, we only use the sleep timer and assume that the underlying android implementation cares for underruns. That's also the key implementation assumption in the start of the stream, when you see the timer there.

For applying on change: AE has a dedicated settings callback, which should be applied whenever some audio setting changes. From this a message is sent to AE, which should then update the setting.

Take care: when in RAW mode AE will automatically call AddPause, which is not producing any values. It just ask the sink to do whatever it wants to do, by giving it the milliseconds with the AddPause call.

Assumption as posted in other PR: android raw sink lower layer produces the pause frames itself.

> For applying on change: AE has a dedicated settings callback, which should be applied whenever some audio setting changes. From this a message is sent to AE, which should then update the setting.

> android raw sink lower layer produces the pause frames itself.

Then this not works well. We could say that there is a bug in an external code, not fix it and tag it as "Resolution External" but this PR tries to provide a simple workaround. It's not perfect but it improves what we have now.
I agree. Could we workaround it here instead: https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/master/xbmc/cores/AudioEngine/Sinks/AESinkAUDIOTRACK.cpp#L935 :-) see also the comment there, hehe.

The ugly details are in this line: 
https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/master/xbmc/cores/AudioEngine/Sinks/AESinkAUDIOTRACK.cpp#L947 

One might ask why the m_pause also gets incremented by the millis. A proper implementation should keep the "original time" and just do whatever it needs to do during the pause. The problem is the following:

Let's assume the sink is in the following state, when pause is pressed:

[data3][data2][data1][data0] -> real hardware

Now we pause the sink, so leaving alone the hardware buffers that you cannot rewrite anymore, we could assume that after the usleep the delay on the sink is still d(data3)+d(data2)+ ... + d(data0), right?

But now the culprit comes. While this might be true for pause during the stream, it is not correct for the start of the stream, as here suddenly the "preheating" won't work.

Maybe the "pause" behaviour might be fixed if you just remove the m_pause += millis; I don't remember anymore for stream start ... or a better concept here.

Edit:
Maybe try:
```
usleep(millis * 500);
m_pause_ms += (millis / 2);
```
this might half the error in general ...

On IEC it works like this:

Sink state:
[D3][D2][D1][D0] -> hardware

Create IEC Frame with silence -> add it:
[S0][D3][D2][D1][D0] -> hardware

When sink is blocking, e.g. all periods on the hw, the AddPacket will block, else it will return immediately, but the GetDelay will reflect the change. In IEC mode the sink is never paused and it is controlled by adding pause frames, which will slowly sync when new data is added again.

For RAW this is sadly not so easily possible. Cause we "pause" the sink, that means it is not consuming the packages it already has, they stay in the queue and sink->pause will just cause that the data already on the sink is played a bit "later" after the sink is ->play() again.

So - at the end it will have the same effect, but working "from the front" while the IEC approach works from the back. Given (!) that the underlaying RAW implementation properly creates pause bursts when in pause state ...

Therefore I think _not adding_ millis to m_pause when we are already playing succesfully should be done. For playback start, story is different. Cause one needs to still "warm sleep" the sink, but also indicate the proper Delay (from the auto generated pause bursts) to AE.

Yeah - I sadly remember the flaws of the RAW API and its design flaws when you really want to haver perfect A/V sync.

Code is here: https://github.com/fritsch/xbmc/commits/at26 - I took over the silence fix from @thexai - but left out the AddPause removal code - as this is wrong by design (while the design sucks ;-)) let me explain you why:

When kodi plays a video with audio it basically has "two clocks". One for audio, one for video and both need to be in sync to each other, if not - video might go in front or in back. VideoPlayer carefully measures this offset and when the offset gets too large kindly asks audio to "try again". This is what you see in your log with the large offset. Audio is then muted and when audio reports it is back in sync, then it's enabled again.

Now come the bloody details:
- What can you do when you have RAW PT packages and video is ahead or in front?
Answer: Not much. Cause compared to the IEC passthrough, where we just can create "empty containers (IEC frames)" that have internal information: I am a pause burst - having same data length as other packages transmitted, you cannot do that with the "content" of the such a container, which is RAW.

Therefore we rely on Android to properly care for such "underruns", when you don't add data, you will underrun. VideoPlayer for RAW format will therefore call AddPause(amount millis). But what can we do with that amount of millis? Also again not much. We could - if the sink buffer is full "sleep" them out, so that the audio queue is reduced during that time in combination with pausing the internal android sink. In other words: we "pause" the sink, so that the content which is already "in the sink" will come, when resumed, "amount" of ms later -> we are syncing, but relaying on Android to properly care for underruns.

But now - VideoPlayer, out of good reason, does not trust us. It measure the amount it gave us AND it calls us after we got it to measure our Delay. So that means if he give you 300 ms of data and calls you 2 ms later for your delay and you say: it's 5 ms ... then it knows that you are 298 ms wrong -> adjusting starts.

Finally - without a possibility to really "add" data, we need to sleep out the "error" which we track ourselves in the pauseburst timer when adding new packages by AE.

This is what the rather complicated code does that I linked. Let's see how it goes.

I don't disagree, without the packer changes (needed by few new TrueHD blurays) this would not work yet. But this has nothing to do with the Shield Experience workaround, which is not correct and only works cause VideoPlayer does not adjust, cause sink always reports dry.

See the change of implementation here: https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/master/xbmc/cores/AudioEngine/Sinks/AESinkAUDIOTRACK.cpp#L881

This can't be correct, cause the sink continues to compare with the non reduced value here: https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/master/xbmc/cores/AudioEngine/Sinks/AESinkAUDIOTRACK.cpp#L708

Effect: Delay of TrueHD streams will always be "zero" reported to AudioEngine, which is why nothing is adjusted for a long time. Also keep in mind, that for the IEC path, the IEC container is created in a way so that it is equivalent to the audio frames in relation to samplerate. So I don't think the reduced time, e.g. halving TrueHD time is correct on the IEC path.

In my opinion the issue is within the Shield Experience Update and they somehow forgot how to properly sync to 24 * 1000 / 1001 fps :-). When people would downgrade Shield Firmware and revert just the ratio division above, everything should be perfectly fine.

See you next year!

And one more on topic: For me the DD+/Atmos seeking works perfectly fine with my latest changes here. I don't have TrueHD / DTS-HD-MA on my Firetv4K stick, which might need additional changes. What I got in my work break is: https://github.com/fritsch/xbmc/commits/at26 - whoever wants, take what you need to continue working on audiotrack.

> When people would downgrade Shield Firmware and revert just the ratio division above, everything should be perfectly fine.

This I know 100% sure that it does not work because it was already been tested  😒

Basically is v19.3 + Shield old FW 8.2.3 = micro-stutter

And post-fix OK confirmations:
https://forum.kodi.tv/showthread.php?tid=365127&pid=3072958#pid3072958
https://forum.kodi.tv/showthread.php?tid=365127&pid=3073290#pid3073290
https://forum.kodi.tv/showthread.php?tid=365127&pid=3074876#pid3074876

Also for Shield's related AI upscaling issues:
https://forum.kodi.tv/showthread.php?tid=365127&pid=3073521#pid3073521
https://forum.kodi.tv/showthread.php?tid=365127&pid=3075520#pid3075520

To finish a thought: 

All these users who participated in the tests are NOT complaining now..... Why?

The most credible answer is that for 99% of people it just works FINE.

I cannot comment on that - I never had a Shield. Therefore I want to focus again on the code: https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/22341#issuecomment-1372444989 as documented here, this does not work intentional.

issue_context.title: Bug, keep device Alive and send low volume noise broken in Kodi 19
issue_context.body:
BUG KODI 19

Having consulted the forums it seems confirmed that kodi no longer works to "keep audio devices alive" and "send low volume audio"..  my soundbar times out and switches off regardless of both settings being enabled..

Other users users have confirmed Kodi isn't sending low volume audio for them either..

Running latest Kodi 19 .4.0 on Ubuntu 20.04.4 LTS

I have good normal working sound output via HDMI (using pulse audio from my Caicos HDMI audio (Radeon HD 7450), but even setting it directly to alsa or direct to HDMI Caicos changes nothing..

I'm using ARC to send the sound through TV to my Panasonic soundbar, nothing has changed with my hardware or TV soindbar setup since Kodi 17..

I'm no longer able to keep the soundbar alive with the "Keep audio device alive option" on always, and/or ticking "the send low volume sound" option..

 it used to be fine with kodi 18... Now if I leave a video paused or am in the home screen doors more than about 10 minutes, the soundbar goes into standby...

If I turn the soundbar to max volume when paused I can hear no faint whistle, though maybe it's out of my human ears audible hrtz range?

I've checked my hardware setting in Ubuntu and my pulse logs and the Caicos is still alive and not going to sleep..

Both pulse and ALSA seems to be affected.

Please investigate and fix bug?
comments:
>If I turn the soundbar to max volume when paused I can hear no faint whistle, though maybe it's out of my human ears audible hrtz range?

Afaik this is the case, so you shouldn't hear anything even if your setup is on max volume.

I shortly tested it yesterday night but in master. Output Silence is never called and pulseaudio goes into idle state right away. Same for ALSA. Something got borked on the way. Will recheck with Matrix over the weekend as there are many Literals changes in master which might or might not have timer influences.
Thank you for confirming, hopefully it's an easy fix..

Could you please post a debuglog and I cannot reproduce with latest stable version (Matrix).

I verified the following:
Current master: broken, stops sending silence packages immediately.
Matrix: Working - pulseaudio does not go into standby by itself

20.0.4 is ver old and I can't remember how pulseaudio needed to be set to debugging. On modern Ubuntu it's driven by a user session and you can set it to debug in /etc/pulse/daemon.conf and use journalctl --user -a -u pulseaudio

@lrusak  Could you please have another look at your "Lexical" changes. I have the feeling that the timers inside ActiveAESink don't work anymore as they should. I cannot spot another. You will see the sink-input even disappearing right away (pactl list sink-inputs). It stay active on Matrix and immediately times out on Nexus. I did not follow the development recently, but as the OutputSilence is not called anymore I don't expect the culprit being the generation of silence packages but rather a timer not working anymore.

Please post the kodi.log - the pulseverbose.log you posted now sadly does not show kodi running / opening a stream ...
The pulse.log only makes sense when kodi was actually running in parallel and the IDLE behaviour was visible - as then pulse log will tell that the stream was marked idle with a timeout. Non of this is visible in your log.

[kodi.log](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/files/8597930/kodi.log)
[pulseverbose.log](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/files/8597932/pulseverbose.log)

Ok new pulseaudio debug log and kodi.log

did this while setting the keep audio alive and the send low volume off and back on, and then running a kodi stream (trailer) pausing it, playing it, stopping it..

If this still doesnt show what you need, someone will have to walk me through step by step what is required//

For that you said, you changed the settings, everything looks good. In kodi.log there is only one time of sink reconfigure (when you swapped the keep alive setting) and in pulse I see that there appears a corresponding idle, which is also okay.

So - in order to properly see what is happening, please do:
Open kodi, set "keep alive to always" and also enable "send low volume noise" (this setting was exactly done cause modern AVRs smelled the zeroes and turned off never the less).

Now - scroll through the menus, with menu sound enabled, so that you actually hear the menu clicks - now wait 15 seconds without doing anything. Now play a menu sound again by moving up / down.

Afterwards please post the pulseverbose.log and the kodi.log, we should see IDLE transition in this break and we should see sink reconfigure right away when you press the very latest time up / down after the break.

I can show you what I mean. Here with "keep alive off" in kodi 19.4:
Mai 01 08:55:53 L380 pulseaudio[249384]: Drain acknowledged of 'kodi audio stream'
Mai 01 08:55:53 L380 pulseaudio[249384]: Requesting rewind due to corking
Mai 01 08:55:53 L380 pulseaudio[249384]: Requested to rewind 0 bytes.
Mai 01 08:55:53 L380 pulseaudio[249384]: alsa_output.pci-0000_00_1f.3.analog-stereo: state: RUNNING -> IDLE
Mai 01 08:55:53 L380 pulseaudio[249384]: Sink alsa_output.pci-0000_00_1f.3.analog-stereo becomes idle, timeout in 5 seconds.

Keep alive on:
Mai 01 08:59:29 L380 pulseaudio[249384]: alsa_output.pci-0000_00_1f.3.analog-stereo: state: IDLE -> RUNNING
Mai 01 08:59:29 L380 pulseaudio[249384]: Requesting rewind due to end of underrun.
Mai 01 08:59:29 L380 pulseaudio[249384]: Requested to rewind 8820 bytes.
Mai 01 08:59:29 L380 pulseaudio[249384]: Limited to 8468 bytes.
Mai 01 08:59:29 L380 pulseaudio[249384]: before: 2117
Mai 01 08:59:29 L380 pulseaudio[249384]: after: 2117
Mai 01 08:59:29 L380 pulseaudio[249384]: Rewound 8468 bytes.
Mai 01 08:59:29 L380 pulseaudio[249384]: Processing rewind...
Mai 01 08:59:29 L380 pulseaudio[249384]: latency = 2383
Mai 01 08:59:29 L380 pulseaudio[249384]: Have to rewind 8468 bytes on render memblockq.
Mai 01 08:59:29 L380 pulseaudio[249384]: Processing rewind...
Mai 01 08:59:39 L380 pulseaudio[249384]: Synced.

If you see the time stamps, you see that above kodi drains immediately and PA becomes idle, while below "nothing" happens for 10 seconds as you see. Means: keep alive works as it should.

For v20 nightlies it drains it always, no matter the setting - but this I cannot reproduce (as you see with 19.4).

[kodi.log](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/files/8599394/kodi.log)
[pulseverbose.log](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/files/8599395/pulseverbose.log)

Ok as requesed, start  logging, start kodi, set audio alway and low volume ON, then move in menu, stop moving, wait 15 secs, start moving in menu, hear sounds, stop logging.

hopefuly this is as needed!!

In fact it looks good. kodi's stream survives all the time until your pulse gets stopped.
The non-working situation would look like this:

Mai 01 19:59:57 L380 pulseaudio[249384]: Hmm, no streams around, trying to vacuum.
Mai 01 19:59:57 L380 pulseaudio[249384]: Freeing input 109 "kodi audio stream"
Mai 01 19:59:57 L380 pulseaudio[249384]: Freed 109 "KodiSink"
Mai 01 19:59:57 L380 pulseaudio[249384]: Connection died.

This you can see when you turn off "noise / always" setting.

Two things come to my mind:
Could it be that your AMD HDMI audio has issues with: suspend-on-idle setting?
https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/PulseAudio/Troubleshooting
You can try to unload that suspend-on-idle. Does that change anything?

I don't expect that to change anything as kodi's stream stays active.
Did your device receive a FW update? So that it ignores the noise?

If you can build kodi from source, you could change the "volume" in GenerateNoise to crossverify.

Oops I had commented out the suspend-on-idle in the pulse default. pa, but I didn't realise it was doubled up in the system.pa as well... BOTH are now commented..

Hopefully that'll solve my issue..

At least maybe we caught the issue with Kodi 20 early, if nothing else.. 

Many thanks for all your help .

I'm having this problem too. Using Linux, alsa only, and Kodi compiled from git. Keep audio device alive is set to Always, and send low noise is enabled. For example, if I start Kodi and let the gui idle for about 2 seconds, my AVR loses audio (the little channel icons turn off). If I press a button the remote, I can see in the log that the audio device is re-initialized. I won't hear any sounds until I press a button again. But then if I idle the gui for a second or two, the AVR loses audio again. It certainly seems like the `keep audio device alive` is broken. Has there been any progress on this? I can create a debug log if it would help.

Yes. Git master is broken. If you can bisect be my guest. I sadly don't have time in foreseeable future.

Stable version works for me. Master only sends noice right before a menu click, which we want to for warm up and then not anymore at all, which is the bug.

Seems to me the idle, silence timer got broken, sink directly unloads again, no matter the alive menu setting.
I'd gladly bisect but is there a specific dir I can bisect to help it along? xbmx/cores/AudioEngine maybe?

Jep, if you want, you can do that. Even ActiveAESink would most likely be enough.

Edit: ./xbmc/cores/AudioEngine/Engines/ActiveAE/ActiveAESink.cpp <- this one.

> Jep, if you want, you can do that. Even ActiveAESink would most likely be enough.
> 
> Edit: ./xbmc/cores/AudioEngine/Engines/ActiveAE/ActiveAESink.cpp <- this one.

I bisected that, had to skip a couple times due to compile errors. Results are:

There are only 'skip'ped commits left to test.
The first bad commit could be any of:
07d579e643503ad7ead066b6abda6ba4b7bb8636
d880bc46165f43e47961720ae2f00c94e56e2da3
ed51cd2245a87236ec603a2faf0530d34ebddedd
We cannot bisect more!
Hehe - thanks much. You just landed on the assumption I posted in my very first reply here. I already pinged the author of all the three patches you found.

+1 am also affected

pretty bad over here since it then triggers these other bug:

https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/21213
https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/20870

Unfortunately is not fixed yet in ARM64 at least (Shield) with keep alive setting = "Always"

It would be nice if someone else could confirm it on other ARM or ARM64 devices/platforms

review_comments: We should be using std::chrono right away here.
I will not rework all Kodi settings API
You don't need to, just use `std::chrono::minutes` initialized by the int returned by the settings.
Or just convert it to milliseconds right away from minutes.

Conversion takes place here:
https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/077c7888fc58c05f27f061e306068cacb95843d2/xbmc/cores/AudioEngine/Engines/ActiveAE/ActiveAESink.cpp#L330-L335

Data is transported by AE Control Protocol as pointer to "raw data" anyway. Even more common data types as `bool` needs re-converted after.
Yea that's fine. So instead of `std::chrono` like I suggested why not drop the conversion completely and just use the int as minutes and convert it later in the line you linked?

> why not drop the conversion completely and just use the int as minutes and convert it later in the line you linked?

- Because `m_settings` stores time in ms and maybe is used in others places or is documented somewhere.
- Because before chrono changes it was like this and this does not cause any problem.
- Because it's not necessary.
- Because there is no advantage in doing this.
- Because only you ask for it.
- Because I don't have time or desire to review where that variable is used the most.
- Because it's PR is mine and I'm doing it.
- Because it can be improved later in another PR (and break new things along the way).
- Because I don't feel like recompiling Android apk. and retest all things.
- Because I want to make as few changes as possible (and make them safe) to be able to backport to Nexus without introducing new bugs.
- Because this PR is a fix and not improvement.

Technically I still don't understand why this is only needed for TrueHD / DDPlus and not for e.g. AC3 - leave alone DTS / DTS-HD. Maybe the adb logcat reveals that this "forces" the sink to pause itself. If that's the case, then the code inside the AudioTrack sink to handle the AddPause calls is just wrong :-).

Do you have an idea why this works and only for TrueHD / DD+?

I think TrueHD and DD+ would require some more implementation or change in AudioTrack RAW specific code. As commented previously this PR is only a workaround to ~fix~ one issue/bug ONLY present in TrueHD / DD+ RAW.

Obviously we can remove the conditions and do the same for all codecs in RAW, but then pause/seek that already works well in the rest of the codecs gets worse.

Probably the root cause is still related to fact in TrueHD  not all audio frames are playable by itself (requires previous major sync frames similar to video codecs requires key frame). On the contrary with DTS you can cut anywhere and play.

> A Dolby TrueHD bit stream consists of a sequence of access units. An access unit consists of an
> MLP Sync (from label mlp_sync to label start in the syntax below) followed by a segment of each
> substream. A major sync is the same as a minor sync, but with additional information contained in
> the substructure major_sync_info(). Major syncs can be distinguished by the fact that the bitfield of
> 32 bits starting at bit offset 32 from the start of the access unit always equals 0xF8726FBA, whereas
> the corresponding bitfield of a minor sync can never take this value.

> There are two types of MLP Sync: the major sync and the minor sync. Each sync contains a header
> and some directory information, as shown in Figure 1. The major sync has an expanded header
> **containing all the information required to start full decoding of the stream**, whereas a minor sync's
> header consists of no more than size and time stamps. To minimize data rate overheads, most
> access units are introduced by minor syncs, **major syncs occurring typically once per 128 access
> units**.

https://developer.dolby.com/globalassets/technology/dolby-truehd/dolbytruehdhighlevelbitstreamdescription.pdf

**AddPause** is only used/implemented for Audiotrack sink, not used in Windows / Linux, etc:

![AddPause](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/58434170/210134904-7d591cf5-5283-4d7f-ab4e-dbd11308ae9e.png)

It's probably a flawed design from the start and a "PackPauseRAW" should be implemented just like in IEC:

https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/939c521a00f72457ce441f3a90910e61962dc213/xbmc/cores/AudioEngine/Utils/AEBitstreamPacker.cpp#L111-L138

Coincidentally or not, there we have a different code path TrueHD and DD+

> Do you have an idea why this works and only for TrueHD / DD+?

> For the AVR it is as if the stream has ended (while it's paused or seeking) and when unpaused it starts synchronizing with the next major_sync_frame.

As said: AddPause is only there to indicate the time of a gap to introduce and fill. Which is done by putting the sink itself to pause(), meaning the android object of the audio track. Also android is the only sink which wants raw pt ... all others use the iec path.

And yes, we should not rely on a non documented behaviour.

Different question: does it also work if you just return from AddPause() in case for Truehd and DD+ after the usleep?
Test it and answer yourself. I can't test it right now.
Same here, sadly ... maybe I will buy a new laptop soon, so that I can compile kodi in under 3 hours again :-)
